journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
title: Energy intake and appetite are suppressed by glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in obese men.
population: Obese male subjects with BMI 45.5 ± 2.3 kg/m2
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) at 0.75 pmol/kg/min for 8 hours
comparison: Intravenous saline infusion
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at lunch (12:00 h) and dinner (16:00 h)
outcomes_secondary: Appetite sensations using visual analogue scales (VAS) immediately before and after meals and hourly in-between; blood samples for analysis of glucose, insulin, C-peptide, GLP-1 and peptide YY; gastric emptying after breakfast and lunch using paracetamol absorption technique
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such; classification based on study objective. Cross-over design used.
annotation_notes: Small crossover study with only male subjects (8 obese male subjects explicitly stated). Single-day intervention with 8-hour GLP-1 infusion; no long-term follow-up reported.

title: Continuous subcutaneous infusion of glucagon-like peptide 1 lowers plasma glucose and reduces appetite in type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) continuous subcutaneous infusion at 2.4 pmol/kg/min for 48 hours
comparison: Saline subcutaneous infusion for 48 hours
outcomes_primary: Appetite measures during fixed energy intake; plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: Insulin; glucagon; postprandial lipidemia (triglycerides, free fatty acids); blood pressure; heart rate; basal metabolic rate; C-peptide; hunger; prospective food intake; satiety; fullness; side effects
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=6). Crossover design with randomized order. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes listed based on order of mention in methods.
annotation_notes: Very small crossover study (n=6). Sex distribution not reported.

journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
title: Inhibition of sham feeding-stimulated human gastric acid secretion by glucagon-like peptide-2.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: GLP-2 infused intravenously at a rate of 0.8 pmol/kg x min during sham feeding
comparison: Saline infusion during sham feeding
outcomes_primary: Gastric acid secretion
outcomes_secondary: Gastric volume, gastric osmolarity, plasma concentrations of GLP-2, GLP-1, gastrin, cholecystokinin, and secretin
extraction_notes: Crossover design with each volunteer studied twice on separate days. Sample size is 8 participants. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; listed based on study focus. Duration of infusion and sham feeding period not explicitly stated.
annotation_notes: This is a mechanistic/physiological study in healthy volunteers using crossover design, not a therapeutic trial. GLP-2 studied (not GLP-1 agonist). Small sample size (n=8). Sex composition not reported.

title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide 1(7-36)amide in insulin-treated patients with diabetes mellitus secondary to chronic pancreatitis.
population: Patients with diabetes mellitus secondary to chronic pancreatitis; insulin-treated (9 patients) or sulfonylurea-treated (1 patient); also included normal subjects as comparators
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide 1(7-36)amide (GLP-1) administered intravenously at doses of 0.4 or 1.2 pmol/min/kg body weight for 4 hours in the fasting state
comparison: Saline infusion
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included blood glucose, plasma C-peptide, and plasma glucagon levels. Small sample size (n=10 patients, n=5 normal subjects). Study design appears to be within-subject comparison rather than parallel group RCT.
annotation_notes: Small mechanistic study with 10 patients and 5 normal subjects. Crossover design with saline vs two GLP-1 doses. Single 4-hour infusion session, not a long-term treatment trial.

title: Effect of glucagon on carbohydrate-mediated secretion of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-36 amide) (GLP-1).
population: Healthy men aged 23.6 years (mean) with body mass index of 24.0 kg/m2
intervention: Intravenous infusion of glucagon with 100 g oral carbohydrate load containing 1.5 g paracetamol, measured over 6 hours
comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline with 100 g oral carbohydrate load containing 1.5 g paracetamol
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=6). Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Primary and secondary outcomes not distinguished in abstract; measured outcomes include plasma glucose, GIP, GLP-1, insulin, and paracetamol concentrations (as marker of gastric emptying). Glucagon dose, rate, and duration of infusion not specified.
annotation_notes: Study conducted in healthy men only (6 participants). Crossover design with glucagon vs saline infusion. This is a mechanistic study examining glucagon's effect on incretin hormones, not a therapeutic trial.

journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
title: Effects of intraduodenal glucose and fructose on antropyloric motility and appetite in healthy humans.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of 25% fructose at 2 ml/min for 90 min
comparison: Intraduodenal infusion of 25% glucose at 2 ml/min for 90 min; Intraduodenal infusion of 0.9% saline at 2 ml/min for 90 min
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included antropyloric pressures, blood glucose, plasma insulin, gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and food intake at buffet meal. annotation_notes: This is a physiological study in healthy volunteers examining GLP-1 as an outcome measure, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist therapeutic trial. Study compares intraduodenal fructose vs glucose vs saline infusions. Sex of participants not reported.

journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 on energy expenditure and substrate metabolism in humans.

comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)

Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; classification based on study objectives. Energy expenditure measured using ventilated hood system for 4 hours after standard breakfast.
annotation_notes: Study enrolled only healthy men (0% female). This was a metabolic/physiological study, not a therapeutic trial. Cross-over design with GLP-1 infusion vs saline.

title: Influence of acarbose on post-prandial insulin requirements in patients with Type 1 diabetes.
population: Patients with Type 1 diabetes (T1DM)
intervention: Acarbose 100 mg administered orally with a standardised meal
comparison: Placebo administered with a standardised meal
outcomes_primary: Insulin requirement for maintenance of normoglycaemia over 3 hours following meal, assessed using closed-loop insulin infusion system (artificial pancreas, Biostator)
outcomes_secondary: Post-prandial triglyceride levels; glucagon levels; gastrointestinal peptide levels including gastric inhibitory polypeptide (AUC, Cmax, tmax); gastric emptying; oxidative glucose metabolism; blood glucose control
extraction_notes: Cross-over study design with 10+/-3 days washout period between treatments. Blood glucose was normalised before each assessment. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but appears to be insulin requirement based on stated primary objective.
annotation_notes: Cross-over study design with 10-day washout period. Study drug is acarbose, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Follow-up duration per period appears to be 3 hours post-meal but overall study duration not clearly stated.

title: Short-term treatment with GLP-1 increases pulsatile insulin secretion in Type II diabetes with no effect on orderliness.
population: Type II (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes mellitus patients (n=8)
intervention: GLP-1 infusion at 1.2 pmol/l × kg⁻¹ × min⁻¹ with plasma glucose clamped at initial concentration by variable glucose infusion
comparison: Saline infusion
outcomes_primary: Pulsatile insulin secretion (secretory burst mass, secretory burst amplitude), basal insulin secretion, fraction of insulin delivered in pulses

extraction_notes: Randomised cross-over design with each patient studied on 2 separate days. Duration of GLP-1/saline infusion not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.
annotation_notes: Small mechanistic crossover study examining insulin secretion patterns. Short-term infusion study with saline as comparator. Exact duration of infusion not specified in abstract.

title: No effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 on short-term satiety and energy intake in man.
population: Non-obese male subjects
intervention: GLP-1 infusion (1.2 pmol/kg per min) for 1 hour
comparison: Saline infusion for 1 hour
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying of a 400 ml water load; energy intake from ad libitum buffet meal
outcomes_secondary: Self-assessment of hunger and satiety using behavioural self-rating scales; circulating GLP-1 concentrations; circulating insulin levels; glucose levels
extraction_notes: Randomized single-blind within-subject crossover design. Sample size is 10 subjects. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; classification based on prominence in methods description.
annotation_notes: Study explicitly enrolled only male subjects (10 non-obese male subjects). This is a short-term mechanistic study examining acute effects of GLP-1 infusion on gastric emptying and satiety, not a traditional therapeutic RCT.

journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
title: Diet-induced change in fatty acid composition of plasma triacylglycerols is not associated with change in glucagon-like peptide 1 or insulin sensitivity in people with type 2 diabetes.
population: Overweight people with type 2 diabetes
intervention: High-MUFA diet (20.3% of total energy) for 24 days; High-PUFA diet (13.4% of total energy) for 24 days
comparison: Crossover comparison between high-MUFA and high-PUFA isoenergetic diets
outcomes_primary: Insulin sensitivity measured by short-insulin-tolerance test; plasma triacylglycerol linoleic-oleic acid ratio (L:O); phospholipid L:O
outcomes_secondary: Total to HDL cholesterol ratio; fasting and postprandial incremental area under the curve for glucose, insulin, triacylglycerol, nonesterified fatty acids, and GLP-1
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification inferred from study objective and reporting emphasis. Sample size is 9 participants.
annotation_notes: Crossover design comparing high-MUFA vs high-PUFA diets; not a GLP-1 agonist drug trial but rather measuring endogenous GLP-1 response to dietary interventions; very small sample size (n=9)

title: Circulating levels of incretin hormones and amylin in the fasting state and after oral glucose in GH-deficient patients before and after GH replacement: a placebo-controlled study.
population: 24 GH-deficient adults
intervention: Daily evening injections of 2 IU GH/m² for 4 months
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of GLP-1 (fasting and incremental response during OGTT), plasma concentrations of GIP (fasting and incremental response during OGTT), total amylin concentrations, non-glycosylated amylin concentrations (fasting and incremental response during OGTT), plasma glucose concentrations (fasting and after OGTT), plasma insulin concentrations (fasting and after OGTT), ratio between amylin and insulin
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Sample size is small (n=24). GH dose unit appears to be per body surface area (m²).
annotation_notes: Study focuses on GH replacement effects on incretin hormones in GH-deficient adults; GLP-1 is measured as outcome but not used as intervention

title: Glucagon-like peptide 1 increases secretory burst mass of pulsatile insulin secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes and impaired glucose tolerance.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients and subjects with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT); studied in fasting state
intervention: Exogenous GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) administered intravenously at 1.2 pmol/kg/min, started at 10:00 PM the evening before and continued during study
comparison: Placebo (crossover design in diabetic and IGT subjects); healthy volunteers studied with placebo only as reference comparison group
outcomes_primary: Pulsatile insulin secretion characterized by deconvolution, autocorrelation, and spectral analysis; insulin secretory burst mass; amplitude of pulsatile insulin secretion; burst frequency; approximate entropy (degree of randomness)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations; period (lag time) between subsequent maxima of insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: Small sample sizes (8 per group). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract. Healthy volunteers were not randomized to GLP-1 condition, only studied with placebo as reference.
annotation_notes: Crossover design with 8 T2D patients, 8 IGT subjects, and 8 healthy volunteers. Study duration appears to be acute (60 min blood sampling) but overall follow-up not clearly stated. Healthy volunteers only received placebo, not GLP-1.

title: Effect of metformin on glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and leptin levels in obese nondiabetic subjects.
population: Obese nondiabetic male patients (n=20 total: 10 treatment, 10 control)
intervention: Metformin 2,550 mg/day for 14 days
comparison: Untreated obese control subjects
outcomes_primary: GLP-1(7-36)amide/(7-37) levels before and after oral glucose load during euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp
outcomes_secondary: Leptin levels before and after oral glucose load; GLP-1(7-36)amide degradation in human plasma and buffer solution containing dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP-IV)
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract; classification based on study objectives. Sample size small (n=10 per group).
annotation_notes: Study explicitly states 'obese nondiabetic male patients' - 0% female. This is a mechanistic study of metformin's effect on GLP-1, not a GLP-1 agonist trial. 10 treated patients compared with 10 untreated control subjects.

title: Additive glucose-lowering effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 and metformin in type 2 diabetes.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients
intervention: Combination therapy with metformin (1,500 mg daily orally) and GLP-1 (continuous subcutaneous infusion of 2.4 pmol x kg(-1) x min(-1)) for 48 h
comparison: Metformin monotherapy (1,500 mg daily orally for 48 h); GLP-1 monotherapy (continuous subcutaneous infusion of 2.4 pmol x kg(-1) x min(-1) for 48 h); No treatment
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma glucose; 24-h mean plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma insulin; C-peptide; Glucagon; Appetite scores
extraction_notes: Crossover design with three treatment periods. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from main results focus. Sample size is small (n=7). Study described as semiblinded.
annotation_notes: Small crossover study with 7 patients. Trial phase not reported. Sex distribution not reported. Comparator type classified as dose comparison due to crossover design comparing metformin vs GLP-1 vs combination.

journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
title: The effect of physiological levels of glucagon-like peptide-1 on appetite, gastric emptying, energy and substrate metabolism in obesity.

intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at physiological dose
comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Study design was placebo-controlled, randomized, single-blinded, cross-over. Sample size: 18 participants.
annotation_notes: Study enrolled only men (18 obese men). Cross-over design with acute infusion study; no long-term follow-up duration reported.

title: Antidiabetogenic action of glucagon-like peptide-1 related to administration relative to meal intake in subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with oral sulphonylureas
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) 17 nmol administered as 3-hour stepwise infusion started at onset of standard meal (550 kCal) (A), or at 30 minutes after meal start (B), or at 60 minutes after meal start (C)
comparison: Placebo (control meal)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included postprandial glycaemia, postprandial insulin levels, postprandial glucagon levels, and gastric emptying (paracetamol test). Crossover design with random assignment to treatment sequence. Small sample size (n=8).
annotation_notes: Small crossover study with 4 women and 4 men. Follow-up duration not explicitly stated; acute infusion study with 3-hour observation periods.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 infusion must be maintained for 24 h/day to obtain acceptable glycemia in type 2 diabetic patients who are poorly controlled on sulphonylurea treatment.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients poorly controlled on sulfonylurea treatment, hospitalized
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) continuous infusion at 4 or 8 ng/kg/min for either 16 or 24 hours per day for 7 days
comparison: Placebo infusion
outcomes_primary: Change in average glucose (area under the curve for day 7 minus AUC for day 0 divided by 24 h)
outcomes_secondary: 24-h profiles of glucose, glucagon, and insulin; nocturnal and fasting plasma glucose levels; insulin AUC; glucagon AUC; adverse events; clinical chemistry and hematology
extraction_notes: Multiple active treatment arms with different doses and durations (4 ng/kg/min and 8 ng/kg/min; 16 h and 24 h). Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such; inferred from main efficacy analysis.
annotation_notes: Trial phase not reported. Female enrollment percentage not reported. Dose comparison study with multiple GLP-1 doses (4 and 8 ng/kg/min) and infusion durations (16 and 24 h) compared against placebo.

journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology

outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying determined by scintigraphy
outcomes_secondary: Plasma responses of gut hormones including insulin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), CCK, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and peptide YY (PYY)

annotation_notes: Crossover design study in healthy subjects examining acarbose's effect on gastric emptying and gut hormones. Not a GLP-1 agonist trial - study measures endogenous GLP-1 response to acarbose. Sample size not reported. Studies performed with and without acarbose in random order at least 1 week apart.

journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-37) augments insulin-mediated glucose uptake in elderly patients with diabetes.

comparison: Control study with glucose and insulin infusion alone (euglycemic insulin clamp without GLP-1)
outcomes_primary: Glucose disposal rate (Rd) measured using tritiated glucose methodology
outcomes_secondary: Glucose production rate (Ra), insulin values, glucose values
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Crossover design with subjects undergoing both studies in random order. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; classified based on study objectives.
annotation_notes: Small crossover study with 8 elderly patients. Sex distribution not reported. Each subject served as their own control receiving both GLP-1 and control infusions in random order.

title: Bedtime administration of NN2211, a long-acting GLP-1 derivative, substantially reduces fasting and postprandial glycemia in type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes

outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma glucose; meal-related area under the curve for glucose
outcomes_secondary: Insulin secretory rates (ISR); plasma glucagon; gastric emptying (assessed by 3-ortho-methylglucose AUC); insulin concentration profiles during glucose pulse entrainment; pharmacokinetic parameters (T1/2, Tmax); gastrointestinal side effects
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=11). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification inferred from study objectives. Crossover design with single-dose administration.
annotation_notes: Small crossover study with single dose administration. Blood sampling extended up to 63 h for pharmacokinetic assessment. Sex distribution of 11 participants not reported.

journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition

annotation_notes: This is a mechanistic/physiological study in healthy volunteers examining postprandial responses to different grain products, not a therapeutic RCT. GLP-1 is measured as an outcome, not administered as intervention.

title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1(7-36)amide on motility and sensation of the proximal stomach in humans.

outcomes_secondary: Perception of gastric distension (sensation score during isobaric distension), perception score related to corresponding bag volume, plasma GLP-1 immunoreactivity
extraction_notes: Crossover design with three conditions administered on separate days in random order. Sample size is 11 participants. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes listed based on study aims.
annotation_notes: Study explicitly states 'eleven healthy male volunteers' - 0% female enrollment. This is a crossover physiology study, not a therapeutic trial. Each participant received saline and both GLP-1 doses on separate days in random order.

journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
title: Effect of GLP-1 on gastric volume, emptying, maximum volume ingested, and postprandial symptoms in humans.

title: Impaired beta-cell function, incretin effect, and glucagon suppression in patients with type 1 diabetes who have normal fasting glucose.
population: Subjects with type 1 diabetes manifested by glucose >11.1 mmol/l 120 min after an oral glucose load but with normal fasting glucose levels, compared to age-matched nondiabetic control subjects
comparison: Age-matched nondiabetic control subjects
extraction_notes: This is not a randomized controlled trial but rather an observational/physiological study comparing metabolic characteristics between type 1 diabetes patients with a specific phenotype and healthy controls. No intervention was administered; the study examined parameters of islet hormone secretion and glucose disposal. Outcomes measured included fasting glucose, insulin, glucagon values, insulin secretory response to intravenous arginine, first-phase insulin response, glucose potentiation of insulin response, incretin effect, GLP-1 and GIP levels, glucagon suppression, glucose effectiveness, and insulin sensitivity.
annotation_notes: This appears to be a metabolic characterization study comparing patients with type 1 diabetes to control subjects, not a randomized controlled trial of a GLP-1 receptor agonist intervention. GLP-1 and GIP are measured as biomarkers, not administered as treatments. No enrollment numbers, sex distribution, or trial phase reported.

title: The pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety and tolerability of NN2211, a new long-acting GLP-1 derivative, in healthy men.

outcomes_secondary: Adverse events, vital signs, ECG parameters, physical examination, safety laboratory parameters, diuresis, packed cell volume
extraction_notes: This is a phase I dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers rather than a therapeutic trial in patients. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; outcomes listed based on stated study aims.
annotation_notes: Study conducted in healthy male subjects only (no females enrolled). Enrollment calculated as 6 subjects × 5 dose levels = 30 total. NN2211 is liraglutide precursor. This is a Phase 1 PK/PD study but phase not explicitly stated.

journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and tolerability of a single-dose of NN2211, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide 1 derivative, in healthy male subjects.

annotation_notes: Study exclusively enrolled healthy male subjects as stated in title and methods. Enrollment calculated as 8 dose levels × 8 subjects = 64 total. This is a Phase 1 PK/PD study in healthy volunteers, not a therapeutic trial.

title: Plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) responses to duodenal fat and glucose infusions in lean and obese men.

annotation_notes: Study included only men (lean vs obese comparison). This is a physiological/mechanistic study examining GLP-1 response to nutrient infusions rather than a therapeutic drug trial. Crossover design with glucose and fat infusions on separate days.

title: The effects of miglitol on glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion and appetite sensations in obese type 2 diabetics.

annotation_notes: Small crossover study with only 8 obese type-2-diabetic women. Study examines miglitol (an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) effect on GLP-1 secretion rather than a GLP-1 receptor agonist trial.

journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
title: High-fat diet effects on gut motility, hormone, and appetite responses to duodenal lipid in healthy men.

intervention: Liraglutide (human GLP-1 analog) 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, or 0.9 mg once daily subcutaneously for 14 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, postprandial (0-3h) glucose excursion, postprandial insulin secretion, beta-cell function (HOMA-beta), body weight, hypoglycemic events, liraglutide antibody development
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from emphasis in results. OADs were discontinued with washout before randomization. Route of administration not explicitly stated but liraglutide is typically subcutaneous.
annotation_notes: Trial phase not explicitly stated. Female percentage not reported. Multiple dose levels (0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9mg) compared against placebo.

title: Appetite-related gut peptides, ghrelin, PYY, and GLP-1 in obese women with and without binge eating disorder (BED).
population: Obese premenopausal women with and without binge eating disorder (BED)
intervention: Randomized cognitive behavior and dietary intervention
comparison: Obese BED versus obese nonBED groups
outcomes_primary: Plasma concentrations of gut peptides (ghrelin, PYY, GLP-1) pre and post meal ingestion
outcomes_secondary: Ratings of hunger and fullness; ghrelin normalization following intervention
extraction_notes: This appears to be primarily a cross-sectional comparison study with a subsequent intervention component. The intervention details (duration, specific protocol) are not specified. The randomization mentioned refers to a subsequent treatment phase, but the main study design compares two groups of obese women. Limited detail on the cognitive behavior and dietary intervention protocol.
annotation_notes: This is primarily an observational/mechanistic study measuring gut peptides, not a traditional RCT of GLP-1 as intervention. GLP-1 was measured as an outcome, not administered as treatment. The intervention mentioned was cognitive behavior and dietary intervention, not GLP-1 agonist.

journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
title: Tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the once-daily human GLP-1 analog liraglutide in Japanese healthy subjects: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-escalation study.
population: Healthy Japanese men
intervention: Liraglutide, subcutaneous injection to abdomen, once daily in the morning, stepped dose titration starting at 5 microg/kg increasing to 10, then 15 microg/kg at 7-day intervals, with further titration to 20 or 25 microg/kg in some groups, for 35 consecutive days
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics (AUC0-24h, Cmax, Ctrough, tmax, t1/2, Vd/F), pharmacodynamics (plasma glucose concentrations, postprandial plasma glucose), body weight
extraction_notes: Phase I study in healthy volunteers rather than patients with Type 2 diabetes; three groups with different maximum doses (15, 20, or 25 microg/kg); 6 subjects received liraglutide and 2 received placebo per group
annotation_notes: Study conducted in healthy Japanese men only (0% female). This is a Phase 1-type tolerability/PK/PD study in healthy volunteers, not a therapeutic efficacy trial in patients with diabetes.

title: Effect of exenatide on 24-hour blood glucose profile compared with placebo in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, two-arm, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, 2-week study.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes with inadequate glycemic control despite metformin with or without a thiazolidinedione (TZD)
intervention: Exenatide 5 microg subcutaneous injection twice daily (BID) for 1 week, then 10 microg BID for 1 week (14 days total)
comparison: Placebo (volume equivalent) subcutaneous injection for 14 days
outcomes_primary: 24-hour time-average glucose values
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose concentrations (2 hours after morning, midday, and evening meals); duration of patient exposure to glucose concentrations >7.8 mmol/L and >11.1 mmol/L; preprandial and postprandial concentrations of triglycerides; free fatty acid concentrations
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated as such; outcomes inferred from study objectives and measurements described. Study duration was 2 weeks.

title: The acute impact of ingestion of breads of varying composition on blood glucose, insulin and incretins following first and second meals.
population: Overweight volunteers
intervention: Sourdough bread providing 50 g available carbohydrate, followed 3 hours later by a standard second meal
comparison: White bread, whole wheat bread, whole wheat barley bread (each providing 50 g available carbohydrate)
outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose, insulin, paracetamol (indirect marker of gastric emptying), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample size is 10 volunteers. This is an acute feeding study with crossover design implied but not explicitly stated.
annotation_notes: Small crossover study in overweight volunteers comparing different bread types. Not a drug trial - measures endogenous GLP-1 response to foods rather than GLP-1 agonist administration. Follow-up is acute (single day): 3h after bread + 2h after second meal.

title: Effect of valproic acid on body weight, food intake, physical activity and hormones: results of a randomized controlled trial.
population: Healthy participants
intervention: Valproic acid (VPA); dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract beyond 3-week treatment period
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly designated as primary in abstract
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly designated as secondary in abstract; outcomes measured included: body weight, energy intake (measured at lunch and dinner in laboratory), physical activity (measured with accelerometry), glucose levels, hormones (Peptide YY(3-36), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), leptin, ghrelin, insulin), food cravings, hunger, binge eating, depression
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Specific VPA dosing information not provided. Study appears to be mechanistic rather than clinical efficacy trial.
annotation_notes: This study examines valproic acid, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist; GLP-1 is measured as an outcome hormone, not an intervention. Study conducted in healthy participants to study weight gain mechanisms.

journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1, yohimbine, and nitrergic modulation on sympathetic and parasympathetic activity in humans.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: GLP-1-(7-36) amide, alone or in combination with N(G)-monomethyl-l-arginine acetate (l-NMMA, nitric oxide synthase inhibitor) or yohimbine (alpha(2)-adrenergic antagonist)
comparison: Placebo (saline), l-NMMA alone, yohimbine alone
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated. Outcomes measured included: hemodynamic parameters, plasma catecholamines, cardiac sympathetic and parasympathetic modulation by spectral analysis of heart rate, and muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) by microneurography. Dose, route, frequency, and duration of interventions not specified in abstract. MSNA assessment performed in subset of 7 subjects only.
annotation_notes: Mechanistic study in healthy volunteers examining autonomic nervous system effects. Additional subset of 7 subjects underwent microneurography assessment.

title: Comparison of the effects of a high- and normal-casein breakfast on satiety, 'satiety' hormones, plasma amino acids and subsequent energy intake.
population: Healthy subjects with BMI approximately 24 kg/m2, age approximately 22 years
intervention: High-casein breakfast: custard with casein as single protein source providing 25% of energy from protein, 55% from carbohydrate, and 20% from fat, constituting 20% of daily energy requirements
comparison: Normal-casein breakfast: custard with casein as single protein source providing 10% of energy from protein, 55% from carbohydrate, and 35% from fat, constituting 20% of daily energy requirements
outcomes_primary: Appetite profile measured by visual analogue scale (fullness and satiety scores)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose, insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1, ghrelin, and amino acid concentrations measured over 4 hours; subsequent energy intake at ad libitum lunch offered at 180 minutes after breakfast
extraction_notes: Crossover design implied by randomised, single-blind design with subjects receiving both interventions. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; categorization based on study focus described in objectives.
annotation_notes: Crossover design comparing high-casein (25 En%) vs normal-casein (10 En%) breakfast in healthy subjects. Sex distribution not reported.

title: Efficacy and safety of exenatide administered before the two largest daily meals of Latin American patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Latin American patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus from Brazil and Mexico, taking metformin, sulfonylureas, and/or thiazolidinediones, who consumed <15% of their total caloric intake at breakfast
intervention: Exenatide administered before breakfast and dinner (BD): 5 mcg for 4 weeks, then 10 mcg for 8 weeks
comparison: Exenatide administered before lunch and dinner (LD): 5 mcg for 4 weeks, then 10 mcg for 8 weeks
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline to endpoint
outcomes_secondary: Fasting serum glucose (FSG) level, 7-point self-monitored blood glucose (SMBG) profile, safety (including symptomatic hypoglycemia and nausea)
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Both arms received the same drug (exenatide) with different timing of administration. Caloric intake and meal times were not monitored as noted study limitation.
annotation_notes: Open-label study comparing two dosing schedules of exenatide (before breakfast and dinner vs before lunch and dinner), not comparing to placebo or different drug. Total duration calculated as 4 weeks + 8 weeks = 12 weeks.

title: Effect of exenatide on gastric emptying and relationship to postprandial glycemia in type 2 diabetes.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes on oral antidiabetic treatments
intervention: Exenatide 5 microg or 10 microg administered subcutaneously twice daily (BID) for 5 days
comparison: Placebo administered subcutaneously BID for 5 days
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying of solid and liquid meal components measured by scintigraphy (T50)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose, plasma insulin, perceptions of appetite, plasma exenatide concentrations
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 3 periods; single-blind study; cardiac autonomic neuropathy status assessed but not used as inclusion criterion; primary outcome not explicitly designated but gastric emptying appears to be main outcome based on study objectives
annotation_notes: Crossover design with 3 periods (5 microg exenatide, 10 microg exenatide, placebo). Small mechanistic study focused on gastric emptying. No demographic information on sex distribution provided.

title: Miglitol suppresses the postprandial increase in interleukin 6 and enhances active glucagon-like peptide 1 secretion in viscerally obese subjects.
population: Viscerally obese subjects with relative insulin resistance
intervention: Miglitol 50 mg single dose administered before a meal
comparison: Acarbose 100 mg single dose before a meal; Placebo before a meal
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose; insulin; lipids (triglycerides, remnant-like particle triglycerides, remnant-like particle cholesterol); lipoprotein lipase; interleukin 6; intracellular adhesion molecule 1; vascular cell adhesion molecule 1; active glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Study used a randomized, blinded, crossover design with meal loads tested 3 times within 2 weeks.
annotation_notes: Crossover design study comparing miglitol, acarbose, and placebo. Study focuses on alpha-glucosidase inhibitors with GLP-1 as secondary outcome measure rather than GLP-1 receptor agonist intervention.

title: Effect of two carbohydrate-modified tube-feeding formulas on metabolic responses in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus controlled with diet and/or oral antihyperglycemic medications
intervention: Slowly digested carbohydrate formula (SDC) - tube-feeding formula rich in slowly digested carbohydrate and monounsaturated and omega-3 fatty acids; Diabetes-specific formula (DSF) - lower-carbohydrate diabetes-specific tube-feeding formula
comparison: Standard formula (STND) - tube-feeding formula intended for individuals without diabetes
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose response (positive area under the curve for glucose)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin response (positive area under the curve for insulin); Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) response
extraction_notes: Crossover design with three treatments; all subjects received all three formulas. Sample size n=48. Dose, volume, and duration of tube-feeding administration not specified. Order of primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in abstract.
annotation_notes: Crossover design comparing three tube-feeding formulas; this is a metabolic study measuring GLP-1 responses rather than a GLP-1 agonist drug trial; follow-up duration for each treatment period not specified

title: Exenatide once weekly versus twice daily for the treatment of type 2 diabetes: a randomised, open-label, non-inferiority study.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, naive to drug therapy or on one or more oral antidiabetic agents
intervention: Exenatide long-acting release formulation 2 mg administered subcutaneously once weekly for 30 weeks
comparison: Exenatide 10 mcg administered twice daily for 30 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c at 30 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving target HbA1c levels of 7.0% or less, hypoglycaemia, bodyweight change
extraction_notes: Route of administration not explicitly stated but implied subcutaneous based on drug formulation. Secondary outcomes inferred from results reported but not explicitly labeled as secondary.
annotation_notes: Open-label study comparing once-weekly vs twice-daily exenatide formulations. No sex/gender information reported in abstract.

title: Effects of exenatide versus sitagliptin on postprandial glucose, insulin and glucagon secretion, gastric emptying, and caloric intake: a randomized, cross-over study.
population: Metformin-treated type 2 diabetes patients
intervention: Exenatide 5 microg BID for 1 week, then 10 microg BID for 1 week (2 weeks total)
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg QAM for 2 weeks
outcomes_primary: 2-hour postprandial glucose
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose parameters (AUC, Cave, Cmax), fasting glucose, insulinogenic index of insulin secretion, postprandial glucagon, postprandial triglycerides, gastric emptying (acetaminophen absorption), caloric intake (ad libitum dinner), adverse events
extraction_notes: Cross-over design with 2-week treatment periods. Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; 2-h PPG inferred as primary based on presentation. Caloric intake assessed in subset of patients only.
annotation_notes: Enrollment size derived from evaluable N=61; cross-over design with 2-week treatment periods per arm

journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
title: Pharmacokinetics and tolerability of a novel long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 analog, CJC-1131, in healthy and diabetic subjects.
population: Healthy subjects and Type 2 diabetic patients (after 9-day washout from anti-diabetic medication)
intervention: CJC-1131 (novel long-acting GLP-1 analog), subcutaneous injection, single rising doses: 1.5-20.5 microg/kg in healthy subjects; 1.5-12 microg/kg in diabetic patients
comparison: Placebo (1 placebo per 6 subjects in healthy groups; 2 placebo per 8 patients in diabetic groups)
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (Cmax, half-life), maximum tolerated dose
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics (blood glucose levels measured 7 times daily, meal tolerance tests on day before dosing and Day 3), weight changes
extraction_notes: Phase of trial not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly defined in abstract; categorized based on stated objectives. Specific timing and duration of follow-up not clearly stated beyond Day 3 meal tolerance tests.
annotation_notes: Phase 1 pharmacokinetic/tolerability study. Enrollment calculated: 8 groups x 6 healthy subjects (48) + 6 groups x 8 diabetic patients (48) = 96 total, but this includes placebo subjects within groups. Actual enrollment: healthy subjects 8 groups with 5 active + 1 placebo each = 48; diabetic patients 6 groups with 6 active + 2 placebo each = 48; total 96. However abstract states each healthy group had 6 subjects (1 placebo) and each diabetic group had 8 patients (2 placebo), so 48 + 48 = 96. Revised: 8x6=48 healthy + 6x8=48 diabetic = 96 total. Trial phase not explicitly stated but appears to be Phase 1 based on design.

journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
title: Exenatide pharmacokinetics in healthy Chinese subjects.
population: Healthy adult Chinese subjects
intervention: Exenatide 10 microg by subcutaneous injection: single injection on Day 1, twice daily on Days 2 and 3, and once on Day 4
comparison: Exenatide 5 microg by subcutaneous injection: single injection on Day 1, twice daily on Days 2 and 3, and once on Day 4
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUCtau,ss, tmax, half-life, apparent volume of distribution, apparent clearance, accumulation ratios, linearity index)
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability (adverse events, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, body weight, clinical laboratory evaluations)
extraction_notes: This is a pharmacokinetic study in healthy volunteers, not a therapeutic efficacy trial in patients with Type 2 diabetes. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated; classification based on study objectives.
annotation_notes: Pharmacokinetic study in healthy volunteers, not patients with diabetes. Trial phase not explicitly stated.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of exenatide monotherapy over 24 weeks in antidiabetic drug-naive patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study.
population: Patients aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes, naive to antidiabetic agents, whose disease was inadequately controlled with diet and exercise alone
intervention: Exenatide 5 microg or exenatide 10 microg administered subcutaneously twice daily (BID) for 24 weeks
comparison: Placebo administered subcutaneously twice daily (BID)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary; efficacy measures included: glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting serum glucose (FSG), 6-point self-monitored blood glucose, percentages of patients achieving HbA1c values ≤6.5% and ≤7.0%, weight, homeostasis model of beta-cell function (HOMA-B)
outcomes_secondary: Tolerability measures included patient-reported adverse events, hypoglycemia, and blood pressure
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; all outcomes listed under general efficacy and tolerability measures. Two exenatide dose groups (5 microg and 10 microg) were tested.
annotation_notes: Female percentage calculated from 102 women out of 232 total participants (102/232 = 43.97%)

journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
title: Pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of albiglutide, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 mimetic, in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Albiglutide subcutaneous injection: Study 1 - 9 mg, 16 mg, or 32 mg administered on day 1 and day 8; Study 2 - single dose of 16 mg or 64 mg administered to arm, leg, or abdomen
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacodynamics (24-hour mean weighted glucose area under the curve, fasting plasma glucose, postprandial glucose), pharmacokinetics (half-life), safety, and tolerability of albiglutide
outcomes_secondary: Hypoglycemic episodes, adverse events (headache, nausea), effect of injection site on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics
extraction_notes: Study design described as single-blind dose-escalation study with two complementary studies. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.
annotation_notes: Two complementary studies described: 54 subjects in dose-escalation study and 46 subjects in injection site study, totaling 100 subjects. Trial phase not explicitly stated. Follow-up duration not clearly reported beyond day 9 measurements.

title: Liraglutide versus glimepiride monotherapy for type 2 diabetes (LEAD-3 Mono): a randomised, 52-week, phase III, double-blind, parallel-treatment trial.
population: Patients with early type 2 diabetes mellitus; 746 patients enrolled
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg once daily or liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily for 52 weeks
comparison: Glimepiride 8 mg once daily for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in proportion of glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c)
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated in abstract; interpretation mentions weight, hypoglycaemia, and blood pressure as additional outcomes assessed
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly defined as such in the abstract; weight, hypoglycaemia, and blood pressure mentioned in interpretation section as additional efficacy endpoints. Double-blind, double-dummy design. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT00294723.
annotation_notes: Female percentage not reported in abstract. Trial compares two doses of liraglutide against glimepiride as active comparator.

title: Efficacy and safety comparison of liraglutide, glimepiride, and placebo, all in combination with metformin, in type 2 diabetes: the LEAD (liraglutide effect and action in diabetes)-2 study.
population: Adults aged 25-79 years with type 2 diabetes, A1C 7-11% (if on previous OAD monotherapy for ≥3 months) or A1C 7-10% (if on previous OAD combination therapy for ≥3 months), BMI ≤40 kg/m²
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, or 1.8 mg once daily injected subcutaneously, in combination with metformin 1g twice daily, for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo in combination with metformin 1g twice daily; Glimepiride 4 mg once daily in combination with metformin 1g twice daily
outcomes_primary: A1C change
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change, incidence of minor hypoglycemia, incidence of nausea
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; outcomes inferred from results emphasis. Randomization ratio was 2:2:2:1:2 for liraglutide 0.6mg, 1.2mg, 1.8mg, placebo, and glimepiride respectively.
annotation_notes: Trial has both placebo and active comparator (glimepiride); classified as placebo. No demographic breakdown by sex provided in abstract.

title: Clinical trial: the glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue ROSE-010 for management of acute pain in patients with irritable bowel syndrome: a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study.
population: Patients meeting Rome II criteria for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), regardless of subtype, experiencing acute pain attacks
intervention: ROSE-010 (GLP-1 analogue) administered as single subcutaneous injections at doses of 100 microg and 300 microg
comparison: Placebo (single subcutaneous injection)
outcomes_primary: Proportion of patients with >50% maximum total pain relief response from 10 to 60 minutes after treatment, measured on a 100-mm visual analogue scale
outcomes_secondary: Maximum summed pain intensity difference; time to meaningful pain relief; time to total pain relief; patient ratings of satisfaction with treatment; comparison with previous IBS medications used; safety assessed from spontaneously reported adverse events and measurement of vital signs
extraction_notes: Cross-over design study. Total pain intensity response mentioned in results but not explicitly listed as a pre-specified secondary endpoint in methods.
annotation_notes: Cross-over design study with single injections; follow-up duration for acute pain relief measured in minutes (10-60 min) rather than long-term follow-up; no sex/gender demographics reported

journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
title: Treatment with the dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor vildagliptin improves fasting islet-cell function in subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin or diet, with good glycemic control (glycosylated hemoglobin values of 6.2-7.5%)
intervention: Vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily for 3 months, followed by a 2-week washout
comparison: Placebo for 3 months, followed by a 2-week washout
outcomes_primary: Insulin secretion in response to intravenous glucose and arginine
extraction_notes: No secondary outcomes explicitly defined in the abstract. Sample size was 41 subjects total across both arms.
annotation_notes: This study examines vildagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor), not a GLP-1 receptor agonist. No sex/gender demographics reported.

title: Pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of teduglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) analog, following multiple ascending subcutaneous administrations in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Teduglutide (glucagon-like peptide-2 analog) administered as daily subcutaneous injections for 8 days at ascending doses (10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 50, and 80 mg) using either 50-mg/mL or 20-mg/mL formulations
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics of teduglutide (plasma concentrations, systemic exposure, apparent clearance, peak plasma concentrations)
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability (adverse events, injection site pain)
extraction_notes: This is a Phase 1 pharmacokinetic study in healthy volunteers rather than a therapeutic efficacy trial. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study objectives.
annotation_notes: Trial phase not explicitly stated but described as ascending-dose PK/safety study in healthy subjects, characteristic of Phase 1. Sex-stratified outcomes reported for clearance values in male vs female subjects, but no female percentage or count provided.

title: Reducing dietary fat from a meal increases the bioavailability of exogenous carbohydrate without altering plasma glucose concentration.
population: Overweight subjects with body mass index approximately 30 kg/m²
intervention: Low-fat meal (approximately 530 kcal; 100 g carbohydrate, 1 g fat, 30 g protein) containing [13C]glucose (3 mg/kg body weight); Low-fat meal plus lipid infusion (same meal as low-fat meal with approximately 30 g fat provided via intravenous lipid infusion to match control energy of 800 kcal)
comparison: Control meal (approximately 800 kcal; 100 g carbohydrate, 31 g fat, 30 g protein) containing [13C]glucose (3 mg/kg body weight)
outcomes_primary: Recovery of [13C]glucose in plasma (bioavailability of ingested glucose) during 5-hour period after meal
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentration; plasma insulin concentration; plasma concentration of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP); plasma concentration of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1); plasma concentration of peptide YY3-36 (PYY3-36)
extraction_notes: Crossover design with three separate occasions. Sample size is small (n=9). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; assumed based on study goal statement. Duration of intervention is acute (single meal per occasion).
annotation_notes: This is a metabolic study examining acute glycemic responses to dietary fat reduction, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist trial. GLP-1 is measured as an outcome but no GLP-1 agonist drug was administered. Female count (4 women) provided rather than percentage; calculated as 4/9 = 44%.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tolerability of the dipeptidyl peptidase IV inhibitor LC15-0444 in healthy Korean men: a dose-block-randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, ascending single-dose, Phase I study.
population: Healthy Korean male subjects aged 19-39 years
intervention: LC15-0444 (dipeptidyl peptidase IV inhibitor) capsules administered as a single oral dose at 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, or 600 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Tmax, t1/2, AUC, fraction of unchanged drug excreted in urine, renal clearance), pharmacodynamic parameters (DPP IV activity inhibition), tolerability
outcomes_secondary: Food effect on PK and PD parameters (evaluated in 100-mg dose group with high-fat diet), active glucagon-like peptide-1 levels after standardized meal
extraction_notes: Phase I study focused on PK/PD and tolerability rather than therapeutic efficacy. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study objectives.
annotation_notes: This is a Phase 1 PK/PD/tolerability study, not primarily an efficacy trial. All 60 subjects were healthy Korean men (0% female). LC15-0444 is a DPP-IV inhibitor, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist, though it increases GLP-1 levels.

title: Acute effects of breakfasts containing alpha-lactalbumin, or gelatin with or without added tryptophan, on hunger, 'satiety' hormones and amino acid profiles.
population: Healthy subjects with BMI 22-29 kg/m2, aged 19-37 years
intervention: Subject-specific breakfast containing alpha-lactalbumin (high in tryptophan) with 10% energy from protein, 55% from carbohydrate, and 35% from fat
comparison: Gelatin breakfast (low in tryptophan); Gelatin with added tryptophan breakfast (gelatin+TRP, high in tryptophan) - both with same macronutrient composition
outcomes_primary: Hunger suppression
outcomes_secondary: Glucagon-like peptide (GLP)-1 concentrations; ghrelin concentrations; plasma amino acid concentrations; tryptophan concentrations; plasma ratio of tryptophan to other large neutral amino acids (TRP:LNAA); energy intake during subsequent lunch
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated; determined based on study objectives. Sample size is 24 subjects. Single-blind design specified. Duration of outcome measurement up to 240 minutes post-breakfast.
annotation_notes: This is a dietary intervention study comparing protein sources on appetite, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist drug trial. GLP-1 is measured as an outcome hormone, not administered as treatment. BMI range (22-29 kg/m2) and age range (19-37 years) reported but not sex distribution.

title: Efficacy and safety of exenatide in patients of Asian descent with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin or metformin and a sulphonylurea.
population: Asian patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin alone or metformin and a sulphonylurea
intervention: Exenatide 5 microg twice-daily for 4 weeks then 10 microg twice-daily for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to endpoint
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤7%, weight change, adverse events including nausea, incidence of symptomatic hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Total treatment duration is 16 weeks (4 weeks at 5 microg + 12 weeks at 10 microg). Route of administration not explicitly stated in abstract but exenatide is typically subcutaneous injection.
annotation_notes: Follow-up duration calculated as 4 weeks (5 microg) + 12 weeks (10 microg) = 16 weeks total. No sex/gender demographic data reported in abstract.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tolerability, and safety of exenatide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide in escalating doses: Group A: 2.5 microg single dose then 2.5 microg bid; Group B: 5 microg single dose then 5 microg bid; Group C: 5 microg single dose then 10 microg bid; Group D: 5 microg single dose then 15 microg bid; administered over 10 days
comparison: Placebo (n=2 per group)
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics (t(max), t(1/2), exposure), pharmacodynamics, tolerability, and safety of subcutaneous exenatide
extraction_notes: Phase not explicitly stated but appears to be early-phase pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Single-blind design. All patients received placebo on day 1 before treatment allocation.
annotation_notes: Phase not explicitly stated but appears to be early-phase PK/PD study. Single-blind design. Complex dosing scheme with multiple dose groups.

journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
title: Oral glutamine increases circulating glucagon-like peptide 1, glucagon, and insulin concentrations in lean, obese, and type 2 diabetic subjects.
population: Healthy normal-weight volunteers (LEAN), obese individuals with type 2 diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance (OB-DIAB), and obese nondiabetic control subjects (OB-CON); 8 subjects per group
intervention: Oral glutamine 30 g
comparison: Oral glucose 75 g; water
outcomes_primary: Plasma concentrations of GLP-1, GIP, insulin, glucagon, and glucose measured over 120 min
extraction_notes: No primary/secondary outcome distinction specified in abstract. This appears to be a crossover design with random order administration on 3 separate days.
annotation_notes: This is a mechanistic crossover study comparing glutamine vs glucose vs water effects on GLP-1 secretion, not a therapeutic GLP-1 RA trial. Total enrollment calculated as 8+8+8=24 subjects across three groups (LEAN, OB-CON, OB-DIAB). Study duration refers to measurement period (120 min), not a treatment follow-up.

title: Raisins and walking alter appetite hormones and plasma lipids by modifications in lipoprotein metabolism and up-regulation of the low-density lipoprotein receptor.
population: Men and postmenopausal women matched for weight and sex
intervention: 1 cup raisins per day (RAISIN group), increased steps walked per day (WALK group), or combination of both interventions (RAISIN + WALK group)
comparison: Three-arm comparison: RAISIN vs WALK vs RAISIN + WALK
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: plasma apolipoprotein concentrations (A-1, B, C-II, C-III, E), cholesterol ester transfer protein activity, LDL receptor mRNA abundance, plasma ghrelin concentrations, and plasma leptin concentrations. annotation_notes: 17 postmenopausal women out of 34 subjects (50%). This is a dietary/lifestyle intervention study comparing raisins, walking, and combination - not a GLP-1 receptor agonist trial. Three-arm comparison without placebo.

journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

title: Effects of exenatide plus rosiglitazone on beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity in subjects with type 2 diabetes on metformin.

title: Effect of exenatide on heart rate and blood pressure in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized pilot study.

journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme

title: A psyllium fiber-enriched meal strongly attenuates postprandial gastrointestinal peptide release in healthy young adults.

title: Exenatide versus glibenclamide in patients with diabetes.

annotation_notes: Small crossover study with acute glucose challenge protocol. 8 male and 2 female participants (20% female). Three-way crossover comparing metformin alone, GLP-1 alone, and combination.

journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

annotation_notes: Crossover study with 11 T1DM patients and 12 healthy controls. Single study visit with 270 min infusion period. Multiple interventions compared (GLP-1, amylin, pramlintide, saline).

title: Effect of administration time of exenatide on satiety responses, blood glucose, and adverse events in healthy volunteers.

journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition

journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research

journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

outcomes_primary: Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentration change from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7% (53 mmol/mol); Fasting plasma glucose concentration; Daily insulin dose; Body weight change; Hypoglycaemia rate; Adverse events and tolerability

annotation_notes: Enrollment size 1663 is from main trial; 1311 continued into extension phase. Extension study comparing IDegLira vs insulin degludec vs liraglutide.

annotation_notes: Abstract describes two studies: a single-dose crossover PK study in healthy subjects and a phase 3 treat-to-target study in T2D. Enrollment size and demographics not reported. Phase 3 designation from the diabetes study.

title: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast attenuates glycaemic, insulinaemic and ghrelin response to ad libitum lunch relative to morning fasting in lean adults.

intervention: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast in quantities relative to RMR (1963 kJ), followed by ad libitum lunch 3 hours later
comparison: Extended overnight fast (morning fasting/breakfast omission), followed by ad libitum lunch 3 hours later
extraction_notes: Crossover design with n=35 participants (14 men, 21 women). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured included: lunch intake, total energy intake, blood concentrations of peptide tyrosine-tyrosine, leptin, acylated/total ghrelin, and insulin (assessed hourly throughout the day until 3 hours post-lunch), and subjective appetite measures. The 1963 kJ value appears to be a mean with SD rather than a fixed dose.
annotation_notes: Crossover design studying acute metabolic effects. 21 women out of 35 participants = 60%. Study examines breakfast omission vs carbohydrate-rich breakfast in lean healthy adults, not a disease treatment trial.

title: Once-weekly dulaglutide versus bedtime insulin glargine, both in combination with prandial insulin lispro, in patients with type 2 diabetes (AWARD-4): a randomised, open-label, phase 3, non-inferiority study.

annotation_notes: Female percentage not reported in abstract. Open-label study with dose comparison between dulaglutide doses and active comparator (insulin glargine).

journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology

intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1 7-36 amide) and PYY (peptide YY) in combination at two rates: 0.25 pmol/kg/min (low rate) and 0.5 pmol/kg/min (high rate)

extraction_notes: Sample size is small (n=8). No explicit designation of primary vs secondary outcomes; acid secretion appears to be the main outcome. annotation_notes: Small physiological study in healthy volunteers examining GLP-1 and PYY effects on acid secretion. Not a traditional clinical trial for disease treatment.
